---
title: "Working offline"
---


A site built with Quarto assumes it will be served over http. Open it
from a plain file tree — double-click an `index.html`, or bundle it as
help into a Zotero plugin, where it lives at a `chrome://` address —
and three things die quietly: the interactivity, the search, the math.
`offline/postprocess.py` repairs all three after `quarto render`:

```sh
quarto render mysite
python3 offline/postprocess.py mysite/_site
```

## The three repairs

**quarto.js is an ES module.** Browsers refuse module imports from
`file://`, and with them dies everything the script drives: tabsets,
the scrollspy in the right column, the dark-mode toggle. The repair
rewrites the script into a classic deferred script.

**Search fetches its index.** The search box loads `search.json` over
`fetch()`, which `file://` forbids. The repair converts the index into
a classic script (`search-index.js`) that defines the same data, and
teaches the search to use it whenever the protocol is not http(s) —
which covers `file://` and `chrome://` alike. Search works entirely
in the page; nothing is sent anywhere, offline or online.

**Math comes from a CDN.** Pages with formulas reference MathJax on a
CDN. The repair rewrites them onto the copy vendored in
`offline/mathjax/`, with the relative path adjusted per page depth.
Proof, live on this page — if you are reading it from a file tree,
this rendered without any network:

$$\alpha \;=\; 1 - \frac{D_o}{D_e}$$

After the three repairs the postprocessor sweeps every page and
**fails the build if any reference to an external host remains** —
fonts, scripts, stylesheets, anything. "Offline-capable" is asserted,
not hoped.

## Loud on drift

Each repair matches exact strings in Quarto's output. When a Quarto
update changes that output, the postprocessor **fails the build**
instead of shipping a site that breaks only for offline readers — the
kind of regression nobody notices in an online deployment. This is why
the theme [pins its Quarto version](../dev/maintenance.qmd).

## The proof: a headless-browser smoketest

Repairs that "should work" are not the same as repairs that work.
`offline/smoketest.py` loads real pages from the built site in a
headless Chromium-family browser **over `file://`** and checks, per
page: the scrollspy actually highlights the section scrolled to, the
search button exists and its index is loaded, MathJax rendered its
formulas, Noto Sans arrived, and no CDN reference survived.

```sh
python3 offline/smoketest.py mysite/_site        # or: site/en site/de
```

It autodetects an installed Chromium-family browser;
`QDA_SMOKE_BROWSER` overrides the choice (the CI sets
`google-chrome`). Run it after every build — the zotQDA sites run it
in CI on every push.
